business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (national territory; unitary company registration system for SARL)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China BIT (1984/1985) and France–China DTA (1985, as amended) — relevant where any shareholder or indirect owner is resident in China
France–Hong Kong DTA (2010) — relevant for Hong Kong intermediate holding vehicles
France–Singapore DTA (1974, as amended) and France–Singapore BIT (1975) — relevant for Singapore intermediate holding vehicles
Intra-EU bilateral investment treaties are no longer applicable between EU Member States under the Achmea doctrine; EU free movement of capital rules apply within the EEA

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-60, L. 561-2-2, L. 561-21, L. 561-46 to L. 561-49 and R. 561-1 et seq.; Code de commerce, Articles L. 123-1, L. 123-6, L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-53 et seq.; supplemented by LOI n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (loi Sapin II), LOI n° 2020-1672 du 24 décembre 2020 and ARRÊTÉ du 2 septembre 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed gérant and each natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract of each legal-entity shareholder and corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / equivalent constitutive instrument of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or companies registry in jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (pouvoir) executed by shareholders and proposed managers for the incorporation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in jurisdiction of origin or French notaire for cross-border acts

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft SARL statuts (articles of association) — may be private deed except where contribution of real property or fonds de commerce requires notarized deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, beneficial owner, gérant and authorized signatory against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List (for USD clearing and any US nexus), the French DG Trésor national asset-freezing list, and domestic PEP registers; PEP status assessed under CMF Article L. 561-21, including family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval where any PEP is identified; ongoing sanctions and negative-media screening required before and after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); official name data and RNE extracts via INPI Registre National des Entreprises (data.inpi.fr); historical RCS extracts via Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French law requires all formal filing documents to be in French; foreign-language documents must be translated by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté). The dénomination sociale may include foreign words but must be expressed in Latin script and must not mislead as to the corporate form, activity, or registered office; public-facing documents are additionally subject to the French-language obligations of the loi Toubon.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms requiring prior ministerial or regulatory authorization because they imply regulated financial activities: “Banque”, “Crédit”, “Finance”, “Assurance”, “Courtier”, “Fiduciaire”, “Société de Financement”, “Fonds” and equivalent terms
Terms implying a sovereign or public body: “République”, “National”, “Ministère”, “Préfecture”, “État” or misleading abbreviations
Terms reserved to regulated professions: “Notaire”, “Avocat”, “Expert-comptable”, “Huissier de justice”, “Médecin”, “Pharmacien” unless holders of the relevant title
Terms contrary to ordre public or morality, or terms falsely suggesting a commercial company contrary to the SARL legal form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RNE/INPI or the Guichet unique rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written rectification request with INPI/RNE assistance within 30 days of the refusal notification; if the refusal is maintained, an appeal may be brought before the competent tribunal judiciaire or tribunal de commerce depending on the legal ground, generally within two months of the final rejection; a de novo name may be submitted concurrently to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to CMF/Code de commerce Article L. 123-11-1 commercial domiciliation requirements; the SARL must maintain a real French registered office capable of receiving legal correspondence, and a mere letterbox is insufficient for operational substance; a separate physical operating address is required for the specialty tea salon and associated food-service premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low at a commercial domiciliation address, estimated 5-10% annual probability of unannounced inspection; high for the operating tea-salon premises post-opening, with predicted sanitary and food-safety inspections by the Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) and DGCCRF within the first 24 months of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-26 (SARL); Article 1832 et seq. of the French Civil Code
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI portal) and registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration with the RCS (Déclaration de constitution de société / M0) together with the executed Statuts and legal-publication receipt
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a SARL; the share capital is freely determined by the members. Cash contributions are deposited temporarily with a French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts when no notarial deed is executed, and the bank capital-deposit attestation (attestation de blocage de fonds) must be filed with the Statuts at registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the members of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée in accordance with Article 1832 and the adopted Statuts: the subscription and paid-up allotment of shares to each founder listed in the company register is approved; the registered office is fixed at the address stated in Article 4 of the Statuts from the date of incorporation; Ms./Mr. [Name] is appointed Managing Manager (Gérant) with full corporate authority to represent the company until duly revoked; the capital deposit certificate is acknowledged; and the Manager is instructed to file the incorporation dossier at the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation due diligence and name availability screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Répertoire National des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed corporate name against the INPI database to confirm there is no identical or confusingly similar pre-existing name; collect the founders' identity documents and residential proofs; assess the intended registered office address and determine whether a lease, domiciliation agreement, or written authorization to use the premises is required.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder ID or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an identical protected mark, immediately reserve a secondary proposed name and file a corrected name clause in the draft Statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Statuts and certification of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company members and, if applicable, a French notary public or legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Statuts in French with each member's subscription schedule, contribution values, share-transfer restrictions, and duration; have every member sign each page and close the signature block; obtain a bank attestation evidencing that the cash capital has been blocked or deposited in an escrow account.
required_dossiers: Schedule of in-kind contributions and appraisals, if any
Bank capital-deposit attestation (attestation de blocage de fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal irregularity in the Statuts, secure signatures of all life members, and if the capital attestation is missing, contact the bank to re-issue a compliant certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication and online filing of the incorporation dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites-entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI, and an authorized legal notice journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a constitution notice in an authorized legal gazette in the department of the registered office; upload all required documents on the Guichet Unique platform; certify that the statutory mention of the company's form, name, capital, registered office, and managers is accurate; pay the prescribed filing fee electronically.
required_dossiers: Legal-publication receipt from the Journal d'Annonces Légales
Proof of registered office (lease, domiciliation agreement, or authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, scrutinize the bordereau de rejet, correct the missing or invalid documents, update the legal notice if needed, and resubmit the dossier within the procedural deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the relevant jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Guichet Unique transmits the complete dossier, the commercial registry reviews the statutory legality and compliance of the formation; it allocates the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and enters the company on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; the registry then delivers the official Kbis extract, which constitutes conclusive proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Complete incorporation dossier automatically transferred from Guichet Unique
Valid proof of publication in the legal notice journal
No judicial prohibition or bankruptcy declaration for the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a decision of refusal or requests observations, formally respond within the judicial time limit, rectify the articles if demanded, and request re-examination through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, INSEE, and the relevant departmental authorities (DDETS/DDPP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Kbis is issued, open the SARL's social-security account, register the legal status with URSSAF, obtain the final APE/NAF code from INSEE, compile the share register, adopt the internal decision book, and file the VAT status and occupation permits with the local tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the APE/NAF classification is mismatched or a prefectorial notification is delayed, file a rectification request at INSEE and an explanatory note with the relevant administrative chamber.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DDETS), in coordination with the Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) for food-service hygiene rules
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'exploitation d'un établissement de restauration / salon de thé and Déclaration de manipulation de denrées alimentaires under the HACCP self-check programme; Licence IV optionally added if alcohol-tolerant tea pairings are proposed

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; simple administrative declaration for a non-classified food-service facility under the Environmental Code, subject to local sanitation authority approval
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged exclusively to the municipal sewer network in compliance with Public Health Code Article R.1331-2; grease separators installed where washing operations are significant; commercial waste sorted under French Extended Producer Responsibility rules; ventilation and extraction designed so VOC and particulate emissions remain below the applicable urban workplace thresholds; no open burning or incineration of waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification delivered by the Commission de Sécurité (SDIS) for an Établissement Recevant du Public (ERP) of Type N, Category 5; structural-load inspection confirming public-seating floors and mezzanines meet load-bearing requirements; workplace conformity declaration with electrical-installation certificates; first-aid and two-person health-and-safety training for all serving staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Business formation and registration data are generally submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), which transmits information to the tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SARL and file formation formalities through the INPI Guichet unique. 2. Obtain the SIREN and SIRET identifiers from the Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE). 3. The DGFiP assigns or confirms the French intra-Community VAT number, generally formatted as FR followed by two check characters and the nine-digit SIREN. 4. Select the applicable VAT regime in the tax registration and corporate tax filings. 5. For a foreign entity without a French establishment, apply to the competent non-resident tax service or relevant SIE before undertaking taxable French transactions; a non-EU entity may require a French tax representative unless an applicable exemption or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. 6. Register separately for customs through the French customs administration and obtain an EORI number before importing or exporting goods. 7. Maintain the SIREN, SIRET, VAT number, EORI number, tax correspondence address, bank details, and authorized filing credentials in the statutory tax master file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. A qualifying SARL comprising only individuals and meeting statutory conditions may elect income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu), including the family SARL regime where applicable. A qualifying newly established SARL may also elect temporary income-tax treatment for up to five financial years, subject to ownership, size, activity, and filing conditions. There is no general United States-style check-the-box election. The tax treatment of branches, permanent establishments, partnerships, and hybrid instruments follows French statutory classification and anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directives.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs duties and excise taxes where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France does not provide a universal VAT registration threshold for all transactions. The franchise en base de TVA exemption may generally apply, subject to statutory conditions, where prior-year turnover does not exceed EUR 85,000 for goods, restaurant-type supplies, and accommodation activities or EUR 37,500 for services; enhanced current-year thresholds are generally EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively. Thresholds are subject to legislative amendment and activity classification. VAT registration and reporting may nevertheless be required from the first transaction for imports, certain intra-Community acquisitions, reverse-charge transactions, and transactions outside the franchise regime. A specialty tea lounge must separately assess on-premises food and beverage services, takeaway goods, packaged tea, merchandise, and any ancillary services. The standard rate is 20%, while qualifying food products may be subject to reduced rates depending on their nature, packaging, sale conditions, and immediate-consumption status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic business-to-business electronic invoicing and electronic reporting in phases. All businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Large and intermediate businesses must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026, while small and medium-sized businesses, including a typical SARL, are generally scheduled to issue them from 1 September 2027. Electronic reporting applies to relevant business-to-consumer and international transactions under the same phased framework. France generally uses an approved electronic-invoicing platform model rather than universal real-time invoice clearance at the point of issuance. Invoices must contain required VAT data and be transmitted in an accepted structured or hybrid format through an approved platform or authorized public infrastructure. There is no general physical tax stamp requirement for ordinary VAT invoices. Existing electronic recordkeeping, audit-trail, retention, cash-register, and payment-reporting requirements continue to apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from France or the European Union to a destination outside the EU may be invoiced without French VAT if the seller satisfies the French and EU export exemption conditions and retains reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The usual evidence is a customs export declaration linked to an exit confirmation, together with transport and commercial records. Qualifying intra-Community supplies to a VAT-registered customer in another EU Member State may be exempt rather than technically treated as exports, provided the customer VAT number, transport, and recapitulative statement requirements are satisfied. Services supplied to a business established outside France may be outside the scope of French VAT under place-of-supply rules, subject to customer-status and evidence requirements. Services physically performed in a French tea salon, including food, beverage, hospitality, and cultural salon services, generally remain French-taxable even if the customer is foreign or payment is received from an overseas account. Zero-rating or exemption must not be claimed merely because the customer is non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the seller, purchaser, goods, value, currency, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Electronic customs export declaration containing the applicable customs procedure and Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit result or equivalent electronic evidence confirming that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Packing list and transport document, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier delivery record, as applicable
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery evidence, and accounting records linking the goods to the export transaction
EORI number and any required customs authorizations, licenses, certificates of origin, or product-specific documents
For intra-Community supplies, the customer VAT identification number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List or recapitulative statement

Bank payment evidence may support the commercial file but is not generally a mandatory French export document, and France does not generally require an Inward Remittance Certificate for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export VAT relief. Export proceeds may generally be received through ordinary banking channels, subject to anti-money-laundering, customs, accounting, and transfer-pricing controls. If export evidence is missing, inconsistent, fabricated, or obtained after the fact, the DGFiP may reassess French VAT for the full applicable rate, deny input-VAT recovery where connected records are deficient, and charge late-payment interest currently calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Additional penalties may include a 10% surcharge for late filing or payment, 40% for deliberate non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent conduct, abuse of law, or concealed activity, depending on the facts. Customs infringements may trigger separate duties, VAT, fines, seizure, or other measures under the Union Customs Code and French customs law. Serious intentional tax fraud may create criminal exposure, including imprisonment and fines under French tax-fraud provisions, with enhanced consequences for aggravated conduct and potential separate liability of the legal entity and responsible individuals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (the French central banking and foreign-exchange administration)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As a eurozone member, France applies the principle of freedom of current and capital transactions within the EU/EEA under the Monetary and Financial Code; no general exchange controls exist. With respect to third countries, the Banque de France imposes balance-of-payments reporting obligations but does not restrict remittance of profits by an SARL. Profit repatriation requires a valid annual general meeting resolution, compliance with French statutory reserve and distributable-profit rules, and presentation of standard documentation (distribution resolution, audit certificate where required, and tax compliance evidence). Non-resident shareholding in an SARL is freely permitted; no exchange-control authorization is required for a specialty tea salon operation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement for export proceeds in France. Exporters are not obliged to convert foreign currency receipts into euros nor to do so within any particular timeline. Exporters may retain and use foreign currency freely, provided that the underlying transactions are accurately declared through the sending/receiving bank for Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics and that all settlement documents carry appropriate commercial purpose codes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for EEA-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into France under the PSD2 and ACPR supervision; Low-Medium for offshore/third-country EMIs. An EEA EMI is usable for treasury acceleration, cross-border supplier payments, and liquidity topping-up, but it may not provide commercial banking functions such as credit, guarantees, or deposit-taking, and its funds are not covered by the French deposit guarantee (FGDR). An offshore EMI unlicensed in France cannot independently provide payment services; it must act through a licensed French banking intermediary. A specialty tea salon should therefore treat an EMI as a supplementary rail, while maintaining a primary French banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML provisions (Code monétaire et financier, Art. L561-5) require identity verification from independent and reliable sources. Qualified electronic identification and eIDAS-compliant video-vetting are accepted by some banks for faceless account opening, but French banks commonly require an in-person banking interview or a notarized/legalized KYC dossier for non-resident directors of an SARL. Remote opening is legally possible where the bank operates a certified digital onboarding procedure; however, for non-resident shareholders outside the EU, the practical onboarding success rate is highest with a physical meeting, as banks retain discretion to refuse remote-only opening for politically exposed or geographically dispersed ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity non-EU equity injection without ordinary business rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital subscription agreement; foreign shareholder constitutional documents; source-of-wealth certificates from the passported issuing bank; interim financial projections; declaration of final beneficial ownership; legal opinion from local counsel validating capital formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border tea procurement payments to embargo-prone or high-corruption indices countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier contracts; phytosanitary and food-safety approvals; EU customs SAD/import-licence records; loading and insurance logistics documents; multiple bank confirmation letters; trade compliance screening results against EU consolidated sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive salon turnover pattern inconsistent with monthly SA VAT filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS system audit files; daily cash-count and till balancing reports; bank card acquirer statements; lease and operating-cost invoices; payroll and social-charge declarations; annualized sales forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions with shell-linked intermediaries using opaque remittance corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor corporate registry vignette Kbis; UBO registry extract; in-person supplier due-diligence questionnaire; transport and freight bills demonstrating physical goods movement; documented chain-of-custody payment instructions; confirmation that no cryptocurrency-denominated intermediary is used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the French SARL must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or SEPA credit transfer into the company's French-resident BIC/IBAN account, using purpose code CAPT (capital payments) or EQUI (equity-related) as agreed with the receiving bank. The payment message must identify the share subscription or capital-increase resolution. For initial formation, subscription funds must be deposited with the bank or a notary to obtain the deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds), while subsequent equity contributions may be wired directly to the operational treasury account. The bank will demand legalized constitutive documents, Kbis extract, shareholder resolutions, FATCA/CRS declarations, and evidence of source of funds; all monetary movements are declared to Banque de France via the external-transaction code for direct investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported tea, ceramics, and allied merchandise use (i) SWIFT MT103 plain transfers through SEPA/TARGET2 rails for eurozone counterparties and correspondent banking for non-EUR currencies; (ii) documentary collections (DP/DA) through the French bank's trade desk; or (iii) confirmed irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit subject to UCP600 and ISP98. Such disbursements require accurate commercial invoices, bills of lading, Intrastat/Integrade declarations, and EU sanctions-screening clearance before settlement is released.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for illiquid emerging-market currencies, executed solely to hedge commercial tea-import exposure
Spot-linked simple FX swap for intra-day EUR/USD liquidity management with a French credit institution
Cross-currency swap (EUR/CNY or EUR/JPY) under ISDA-derived French market documentation
European-style European FX option (EUR/USD put/call) purchased for economic hedging of foreign-currency invoice flows
FX forward (Change à terme) aligned to trade settlement dates in EUR/USD, EUR/JPY, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SARL shareholders; minutes retained in the corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may expose the manager to liability and judicial enforcement; no automatic administrative strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The court may order filing under a daily penalty; the legal representative may incur a fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increasing to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeat violations. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December, subject to the applicable tax calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally accrues at 0.20% per month; a 10% surcharge generally applies for late filing or payment, with higher penalties for deliberate evasion or fraudulent conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration update, when ownership or control information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the Guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the relevant change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or update beneficial ownership information may result in injunctions, criminal fines, and restrictions affecting registration or corporate compliance status; there is no routine annual filing where no change occurred.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SARL exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant closing: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional group-company and shareholder-request rules may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) rules applies to individual statutory accounts. IFRS is generally relevant to eligible consolidated accounts and is not the default framework for an individual SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a separate annual beneficial-owner confirmation when no information has changed. The SARL must review its ownership and control data annually and file an update within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must also be documented and reflected in the relevant corporate records and filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and register of shareholder decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,625 per year, depending on city, mail handling, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,625-5,400 per year for a small SARL subject to statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million and independent ownership conditions). Large taxpayers may also face the 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax where turnover exceeds EUR 7.63 million, producing an approximate top effective rate of 25.83%. Available non-statutory incentives include the research tax credit (CIR) and the patent box regime for qualifying acquisition costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) and accompanying schedules 2050 through 2065; filed electronically via the EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) system within the professional space at impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly prepayment instalments for current-year IS (15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December); final settlement effected upon filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closing on 31 December, the return must be filed no later than the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is within three months of the close of the fiscal year. Electronic filing through EFI does not extend the substantive filing period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A - Période d'exercice (date début et date fin)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the exact opening and closing dates of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned SARL whose reference period differs from the calendar year, state the French entity's actual fiscal-year period, even where the non-resident parent operates on a different cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Identification du déclarant - SIREN, SIRET, forme juridique, NAF/APE
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification block containing the registration number, legal form, and primary business classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SIREN/SIRET of the SARL and the NAF/APE code 5630Z for tea salon and beverage service activity. Non-resident directors should confirm the local entity is physically and legally established in France before relying on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ligne AB / AC - Bénéfice / Déficit fiscal
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income or deductible deficit after accounting result, tax re-inclusions, deductions, and loss-relief adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income attributable to the SARL's French business. The entire taxable result, not merely remitted amounts, is subject to French IS. No allocation to the foreign parent is permitted unless a valid permanent establishment structure is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before any tax adjustments, derived from the statutory balance sheet and profit and loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French entity must maintain complete local statutory accounts under French GAAP. Non-resident parent-company recharges not evidenced by transfer pricing documentation must be excluded and reconciled in schedule 2058-A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule listing tax adjustments to accounting result, including non-deductible expenses, including penalties, excessive reimbursements, and transfer-pricing discriminators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure related-party management fees, royalties, and interest are backed by contracts, actual benefit, and a contemporaneous arm's-length analysis. If the French entity has no local file, every adjustment may create exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre 'IS brut' / 'Impôt sur les sociétés calculé' (2065)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the corporate income tax charge, applying the standard 25% rate or the SME reduced 15% rate where eligible, and deduction of foreign tax credits and instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot reduce French IS through treaty where the revenue is attributable to a French establishment. Apply any treaty non-discrimination article, but never claim exemption on French branch profits absent a valid treaty protection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% majoration on the assessed tax under Article 1728 CGI plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%. Intentional understatement exposes the taxpayer to 40% penalty; fraud or obstruction of control triggers 80% penalty. Non-payment after formal notice may prompt enforced recovery and the State's privileged lien over assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% gross dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders absent treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief; 12.8% flat withholding applies to certain non-resident individuals before social levies; 0% available to EU corporate parents holding 5% or more for 24 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the non-resident beneficiary must establish itself as the beneficial owner and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its jurisdiction of residence. The French paying entity must obtain and retain the original TRC and, if applicable, the standard Form 5000/5001 certificate, before or at the payment date. For at-source relief, submit the appropriate attestation to the French withholding agent; if not applied at source, a reclaim may be filed with the French tax administration within the standard two-year claim window for refund of excess withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law generally imposes 25% withholding on IP royalties sourced in France and paid to non-residents, subject to treaty reduction (frequently 0% to 10%). Interest paid to non-resident arm's-length lenders is normally exempt from French domestic withholding unless paid to a non-cooperative jurisdiction, where a 50% withholding can apply. Treaty rates commonly cap interest at 10%, and many recent French treaties reduce royalty withholding to 5% or 0% depending on the IP class and beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (annual revenue or gross assets) for the French entity's Local File; EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue for the Master File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no Economic Substance Regulations barometer in the OFC sense, but economic substance is enforced through the abuse-of-law doctrine (abus de droit), the anti-fraud rule of Article L.64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales, EU ATAD substance requirements, beneficial-ownership tests in DTA relief, and transfer-pricing behavioural tests. A specialty tea salon lounge owned by non-residents must demonstrate real local presence, employees, operating assets, stock management, decision-making, and business risk in France; otherwise the administration may disregard the entity or recharacterise the arrangement as artificial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Concealed French Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a specialty tea salon through a seemingly independent SARL while strategic decisions, contracts, inventory ownership, and revenue recognition are controlled from a foreign parent, with no French substance, or concealing part of the French turnover through unauthorised cash handling or foreign bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% fraud penalty on evaded tax plus monthly late interest at 0.20%; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years under Article 1741 CGI; potential additional penalties for failure to keep accounting records and for mis-declaration of P&L.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in tax evasion may be held jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, penalties, and interest under Article L.267 LPF. Courts may impose a management ban, asset freeze, travel restrictions, and in aggravated cases imprisonment of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting prices for tea products, royalties, management recharges, or financing between the French SARL and foreign related parties outside arm's length range, or failing to maintain a Local File and Master File when thresholds are crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment at the French tax administration's reconstructed profit plus late interest; 40% penalty for insufficient documentation or deliberate misstatement, rising to 80% for fraud; additional potential fines under Article 1735 CGI for failure to produce documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for transfer policies can be made jointly liable for adjusted corporate taxes where deliberate concealment or fictitious documentation is established. This may extend to disqualification from management, travel bans during fiscal proceedings, and criminal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating or maintaining a non-resident-owned French SARL that lacks genuine activity, employees, customers, and decision-making solely to claim treaty benefits or to avoid a higher-taxed jurisdiction, particularly with passive royalty or dividend flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disapplication of the legal entity under abuse-of-law procedure; recharacterisation of transactions; 80% abuse penalty; denial of treaty benefits; possible nullity of certain contracts under civil law; tax reassessment up to the real economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee or de facto directors may be held personally liable for the full restored tax and penalty where the entity is considered fictitious or an instrument of fraud; French courts may impose management bans, prohibitions on residency, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register and file the beneficial owner with the French Trade Registry (RCS), refusing to disclose controlling persons, processing cash payments with no coherent POS reconciliation, or using the tea salon channel to launder third-party funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 30,000 and, for serious laundering, imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 375,000 under Articles 324-1 and 324-2 of the French Criminal Code. Regulatory sanctions may be imposed by the Prudential Control and Resolution Authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL may be personally prosecuted for money laundering and for failing to comply with KYC/AML obligations. In addition, they may be ordered to pay confiscation of assets and be prohibited from managing a business for up to fifteen years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Distribution and Withholding Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends to a non-resident shareholder without applying the statutory 25% withholding, without verifying treaty relief, or distributing profits when the SARL's net equity falls below share capital plus non-distributable reserves.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the distribution as taxable income in the hands of the shareholder; withholding tax reassessment against the SARL; late payment interest; 40% or 80% intentional non-disclosure penalties; civil nullity of the distribution resolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who voted or executed the unlawful distribution can be held personally liable to restore the amounts received by shareholders, jointly with the company, to the extent of company losses. Where fraud is shown, imprisonment and personal tax liability follow.
